1.intro: The Opening — recited in every unit of prayer. A direct conversation between the servant and Allah: praise, worship, and a plea for guidance.

verses.1: We begin with Allah's name — every good act starts by remembering Him, seeking His blessing and help.
verses.2: 'Rabb' means Lord, Master, Sustainer — the One who created everything and cares for it at every moment. All praise belongs to Him alone.
verses.3: Allah's mercy has two dimensions: Ar-Rahman (His vast mercy embracing all creation) and Ar-Rahim (His special mercy for the believers).
verses.4: On the Day of Judgment, no one else will hold any authority. Remembering this keeps hearts humble and deeds sincere.
verses.5: The core of Islam in one verse: we worship Allah alone and seek help from Him alone — no intermediaries, no partners.
verses.6: We ask for the Straight Path — truth in belief, worship, and character. Guidance is our greatest daily need.
verses.7: The Straight Path is that of those Allah blessed (prophets and the righteous) — not of those who earned anger (who knew the truth but rejected it), nor of those who went astray.

2.intro: The longest surah (286 verses), revealed in Madinah. A complete constitution for the Muslim community — faith, worship, law, finance, and family. Named after the story of the cow (2:67-73). Contains Ayat al-Kursi (2:255), the greatest verse of the Quran.

18.intro: The Cave — read every Friday as a light between the two Fridays. Four stories: the youths of the cave (trial of faith), the wealthy gardener (trial of wealth), Musa and Khidr (trial of knowledge), and Dhul-Qarnayn (trial of power). A protection against the trial of the Dajjal.

36.intro: Ya-Sin — called the heart of the Quran. Establishes resurrection, prophethood, and Allah's power through signs in creation. Often recited for the sick and the deceased.

verses.58: 'Peace — a word from a Merciful Lord.' The greeting the people of Paradise will receive from Allah Himself.
verses.82: 'When He wills a thing, He only says to it: Be — and it is.' Allah's power is absolute and effortless.

55.intro: The Most Merciful — 'Which of your Lord's favors will you deny?' is repeated 31 times. A breathtaking journey through Allah's blessings in this world and the next.

56.intro: The Inevitable Event — the Resurrection. Humanity is divided into three groups: the foremost in faith, the companions of the right, and the companions of the left — each group's fate described in vivid detail.

67.intro: Sovereignty — 30 verses that intercede for their reader and protect from the punishment of the grave. Reflect on Allah's perfect dominion over the heavens and the earth.

verses.1: Blessed is He in whose hand is all dominion — true power belongs only to Allah, and He has power over everything.
verses.2: He created death and life to test which of us is best in deeds — life's purpose is the quality of our actions, not their quantity.

78.intro: The Great News — the Resurrection. Opens Juz' 30: short, powerful surahs about the Last Day, meant to wake the heedless heart.

93.intro: The Morning Brightness — revealed to comfort the Prophet ﷺ when revelation paused briefly and he felt abandoned.

verses.1: By the morning brightness — Allah swears by the light that follows darkness.
verses.2: And by the night when it settles — a pair of oaths: after every darkness comes light.
verses.3: Your Lord has not forsaken you, nor does He hate you — the core reassurance of the surah.
verses.4: The future will be better for you than the past — hope is a duty, not just a feeling.
verses.5: And your Lord will grant you until you are pleased — a promise of complete satisfaction.
verses.6: Did He not find you an orphan and shelter you? — recall past favors to trust future ones.
verses.7: And He found you unaware of the path, and guided you.
verses.8: And He found you poor, and enriched you.
verses.9: So do not oppress the orphan — kindness received must become kindness given.
verses.10: And do not turn away the beggar.
verses.11: And proclaim the blessings of your Lord — gratitude in words and in deeds.

94.intro: The Relief — the companion of Ad-Duha. After reassurance comes relief: hardship always carries ease within it.

verses.1: Did We not open your chest for you? — granting clarity, wisdom, and inner peace.
verses.2: And removed from you your burden —
verses.3: Which weighed heavily on your back — sins forgiven, worries lifted.
verses.4: And raised high your remembrance — the Prophet's ﷺ name is honored across the world to this day.
verses.6: Indeed, with hardship comes ease — repeated twice for absolute certainty; ease is guaranteed, not merely hoped for.
verses.7: So when you are free, strive hard in worship.
verses.8: And turn to your Lord with longing.

103.intro: Time — Imam Ash-Shafi'i said: if people reflected on this surah alone, it would suffice them.

verses.1: By time — an oath underscoring how precious and fleeting time is.
verses.2: Indeed, mankind is in loss — everyone loses, except those with the four qualities that follow.
verses.3: Except those who believe, do righteous deeds, urge one another to truth, and urge one another to patience — the fourfold rescue from loss.

105.intro: The Elephant — the year the Prophet ﷺ was born. Abraha marched with elephants to destroy the Kaaba; Allah sent birds with baked-clay stones.

verses.1: Have you not seen what your Lord did to the companions of the elephant?
verses.2: Did He not turn their plot into utter loss?
verses.3: And He sent against them birds in flocks,
verses.4: Striking them with stones of baked clay —
verses.5: Leaving them like eaten straw. The mightiest army is nothing before Allah's will.

106.intro: Quraysh — Allah reminds the tribe of the Prophet ﷺ of His favors: safe trade journeys and security.

verses.1: For the accustomed security of Quraysh —
verses.2: Their accustomed security in the caravans of winter and summer —
verses.3: Let them worship the Lord of this House (the Kaaba) —
verses.4: Who fed them against hunger and secured them against fear. Blessings demand gratitude through worship.

107.intro: Small Kindnesses — condemns those whose worship is hollow: they pray yet ignore the poor and withhold even trivial help.

verses.1: Have you seen the one who denies the Recompense (the Judgment)?
verses.2: That is the one who repels the orphan —
verses.3: And does not urge feeding the poor. Disbelief reveals itself in hard-heartedness.
verses.4: So woe to those who pray,
verses.5: Who are heedless of their prayer — delaying it, rushing it, praying without presence of heart.
verses.7: And withhold simple assistance. Prayer without sincerity and compassion is condemned.

108.intro: The Abundance — the shortest surah. Revealed when the Prophet ﷺ was mocked for having no surviving son; Allah honored him instead.

verses.1: Indeed, We have granted you Al-Kawthar — the abundant good, including a river in Paradise.
verses.2: So pray to your Lord and sacrifice — answer mockery with worship, not grief.
verses.3: Indeed, it is your enemy who is cut off — from all lasting good.

109.intro: The Disbelievers — a dignified declaration: there is no compromise in worship. Equals a quarter of the Quran in reward.

verses.2: I do not worship what you worship,
verses.3: Nor do you worship what I worship,
verses.4: Nor will I worship what you have worshipped,
verses.5: Nor will you worship what I worship — repetition for absolute, unmistakable clarity.
verses.6: For you is your religion, and for me is mine — peaceful coexistence without blending truth with falsehood.

110.intro: The Divine Help — revealed near the end of the Prophet's ﷺ life, signaling his mission's completion.

verses.1: When the help of Allah comes, and the victory — the conquest of Makkah.
verses.2: And you see people entering Allah's religion in crowds — the fruit of years of patience.
verses.3: Then glorify the praises of your Lord and seek His forgiveness. Success calls for humility, not pride.

111.intro: The Palm Fiber — concerning Abu Lahab, the Prophet's ﷺ uncle who fiercely opposed him, and his wife.

verses.1: Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and perish he — his power cannot save him.
verses.2: His wealth will not avail him, nor what he earned.
verses.3: He will burn in a Fire of flame —
verses.4: And his wife, the carrier of firewood (who spread thorns and slander) —
verses.5: Around her neck is a rope of twisted palm fiber.

112.intro: Sincerity — equals one-third of the Quran in reward. Pure, uncompromised monotheism in four verses.

verses.1: Say: He is Allah, the One — absolutely unique, without partner or equal.
verses.2: Allah, As-Samad — the Eternal Refuge: every need turns to Him, while He needs nothing.
verses.3: He neither begets nor is born — free from all human limitations.
verses.4: And there is nothing comparable to Him — in essence, attributes, or actions.

113.intro: The Daybreak — seeking Allah's refuge from external harms. Recited morning and evening with Al-Ikhlas and An-Nas.

verses.1: Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of the daybreak — the One who splits darkness with light can remove every harm.
verses.2: From the evil of what He created — a comprehensive refuge covering all harms.
verses.3: And from the evil of the darkness when it settles — when hidden harms are most feared.
verses.4: And from the evil of the blowers in knots — sorcery is real, and Allah's protection is real.
verses.5: And from the evil of the envier when he envies — the evil eye is real; refuge with Allah shields from it.

114.intro: Mankind — seeking refuge from internal harms: the whispers that corrupt the heart. The Quran closes with this plea for protection.

verses.1: Say: I seek refuge with the Lord of mankind — our Creator and Caretaker.
verses.2: The King of mankind — the true Sovereign over all.
verses.3: The God of mankind — the only One worthy of worship.
verses.4: From the evil of the sneaking whisperer — Satan whispers, then retreats when Allah is remembered.
verses.5: Who whispers into the chests of people — his battlefield is the human heart.
verses.6: From among jinn and mankind — evil whisperers exist in both realms.
